title: Short Squeeze — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A short squeeze occurs when a rising price or difficulty borrowing a security puts pressure on short sellers to close positions by buying shares.
summary: A short squeeze occurs when a rising price or difficulty borrowing a security puts pressure on short sellers to close positions by buying shares. That covering demand can add further upward pressure to the price.

title: Golden Cross — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A golden cross labels a shorter moving average crossing above a longer one, often the 50-day above the 200-day.
summary: A golden cross labels a shorter moving average crossing above a longer one, often the 50-day above the 200-day. It describes historical averages and does not establish that prices will continue rising.

title: Death Cross — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A death cross labels a shorter moving average crossing below a longer one, often the 50-day below the 200-day.
summary: A death cross labels a shorter moving average crossing below a longer one, often the 50-day below the 200-day. This is a lagging price calculation, not confirmation of a future decline.

title: Liquidation Cascade — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A liquidation cascade is feedback in which forced position reductions add price pressure that can trigger further reductions.
summary: A liquidation cascade is feedback in which forced position reductions add price pressure that can trigger further reductions. Venue rules, collateral and liquidity affect the outcome.

title: Fibonacci Retracement — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Fibonacci retracement plots conventional fractions of a selected price swing, often 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8% and 78.6%.
summary: Fibonacci retracement plots conventional fractions of a selected price swing, often 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8% and 78.6%. The 50% level is a common chart convention, not a Fibonacci ratio, and none of these lines guarantees support or resistance.

title: RSI Divergence — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: RSI divergence describes a mismatch between selected price swings and RSI swings.
summary: RSI divergence describes a mismatch between selected price swings and RSI swings. It can be followed by continuation or reversal, so it is not a dependable forecast by itself.

title: MACD Histogram — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: The MACD histogram represents the difference between the MACD line and signal line as vertical bars.
summary: The MACD histogram represents the difference between the MACD line and signal line as vertical bars. It is calculated from past prices.

title: Bollinger Band Squeeze — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A Bollinger Band squeeze describes a narrow distance between the bands relative to a selected comparison period.
summary: A Bollinger Band squeeze describes a narrow distance between the bands relative to a selected comparison period. It reflects lower measured volatility, without specifying the direction or size of the next move.

title: Order Block — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: An order block is a chart-defined zone used in some technical-analysis frameworks; candles alone do not establish actual institutional orders.
summary: An order block is a chart-defined zone used in some technical-analysis frameworks; candles alone do not establish actual institutional orders. Some frameworks use the last opposing candle before a selected directional move; definitions vary.

title: Fair Value Gap (FVG) — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A Fair Value Gap is a three-candle chart pattern where the full price ranges of the first and third candles do not overlap.
summary: A Fair Value Gap is a three-candle chart pattern where the full price ranges of the first and third candles do not overlap. The range need not be revisited and does not establish economic fair value or unfilled orders.

title: Bull Trap — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A retrospective label for a move above selected resistance followed by a downward reversal.
summary: A retrospective label for a move above selected resistance followed by a downward reversal. The pattern alone does not establish buyers’ losses or anyone’s intent.

title: Bear Trap — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A retrospective label for a move below selected support followed by an upward reversal.
summary: A retrospective label for a move below selected support followed by an upward reversal. The price path alone does not establish short positioning or deliberate manipulation.

title: Whale Manipulation — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Whale manipulation is an informal label for alleged manipulation by a large market participant.
summary: Whale manipulation is an informal label for alleged manipulation by a large market participant. Large holdings, transfers or ordinary orders alone do not establish wrongdoing; claims about deceptive trading require evidence and the applicable market rules.

title: Support and Resistance — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Support and resistance are price areas where traders look for repeated buying or selling responses.
summary: Support and resistance are price areas where traders look for repeated buying or selling responses. Past reactions help define the areas but do not prevent a later price from passing through them.

title: Candlestick Patterns — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Candlestick patterns are names for formations built from opening, high, low and closing prices.
summary: Candlestick patterns are names for formations built from opening, high, low and closing prices. Traders use them to describe price action; a formation alone does not establish a reliable reversal or continuation.

title: Head and Shoulders — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A head and shoulders pattern has three peaks, with a higher central peak and two lower shoulders.
summary: A head and shoulders pattern has three peaks, with a higher central peak and two lower shoulders. A neckline connects the intervening lows; breaking it is a chart observation, not a confirmed future decline or guaranteed target.

title: Double Bottom — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A double bottom is a W-shaped chart pattern with two troughs near a similar level.
summary: A double bottom is a W-shaped chart pattern with two troughs near a similar level. A later move above the intervening peak fits the pattern, but does not ensure that a rally continues.

title: Moving Average Convergence Divergence — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: MACD compares exponential moving averages of past prices.
h1: Moving Average Convergence Divergence — Trading Wiki
summary: MACD compares exponential moving averages of past prices. Its line, signal line and histogram describe changes in those calculations; crossovers are not reliable reversal predictions by themselves.

title: Limit Order vs Market Order — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Market orders seek prompt execution at available prices.
h1: Limit Order vs Market Order — Trading Wiki
summary: Market orders seek prompt execution at available prices. Limit orders set a price boundary and may remain unfilled. Choosing an order type involves a trade-off between execution priority and price control.

title: Stop Loss Hunting — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A suspected intentional move through levels where stop orders may be placed.
summary: A suspected intentional move through levels where stop orders may be placed. A price reversal alone does not prove manipulation, identify a trader or reveal actual order locations.

title: Leverage Trading — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Leverage is exposure greater than the supporting equity or collateral; losses can exceed the initial investment.
summary: Leverage is exposure greater than the supporting equity or collateral; losses can exceed the initial investment. At 10x leverage, $1,000 of margin controls roughly $10,000 of exposure. Leverage amplifies both gains and losses.

title: FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: FOMO is the anxiety-driven urge to trade because a price is moving or others appear to be profiting.
h1: FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) — Trading Wiki
summary: FOMO is the anxiety-driven urge to trade because a price is moving or others appear to be profiting. The emotion does not identify a market top or establish a measured win rate.

title: FUD (Fear, Uncertainty, Doubt) — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: FUD means fear, uncertainty and doubt.
summary: FUD means fear, uncertainty and doubt. The label is often applied to negative claims; it does not establish whether a claim is true, false or deliberately manipulative.

title: HODL Strategy — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: HODL is a buy-and-hold expression associated with a Bitcoin forum typo.
summary: HODL is a buy-and-hold expression associated with a Bitcoin forum typo. Holding through volatility can still produce losses; neither a four-year period nor an earlier price history guarantees recovery.

title: Satoshi Nakamoto — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonym used by the creator of Bitcoin, who published its whitepaper in 2008.
summary: Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonym used by the creator of Bitcoin, who published its whitepaper in 2008. Identity and ownership of wallets attributed to the creator remain uncertain.

title: Margin Call — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A demand for additional collateral under an account’s margin terms.
summary: A demand for additional collateral under an account’s margin terms. A broker may reduce or liquidate positions under its rules; a call does not guarantee a response period.

title: Liquidation Price — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A liquidation price is an estimate of the level at which a leveraged position may be closed under a platform's margin rules.
summary: A liquidation price is an estimate of the level at which a leveraged position may be closed under a platform's margin rules. Collateral, fees, other positions and the pricing method can change that estimate.

title: Dollar Cost Averaging — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Dollar-cost averaging means contributing fixed amounts at regular intervals regardless of price.
summary: Dollar-cost averaging means contributing fixed amounts at regular intervals regardless of price. It changes purchase timing and the units acquired; it does not guarantee a lower average cost or outperform a lump-sum investment.

title: Swing Trading — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Holding positions across sessions, commonly for days or weeks.
summary: Holding positions across sessions, commonly for days or weeks. Review schedules and chart intervals vary; gaps and execution risks remain.

title: Day Trading — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Day trading means opening and closing positions within a trading day.
summary: Day trading means opening and closing positions within a trading day. It reduces exposure to overnight moves while retaining intraday price, execution and cost risks; no universal loss rate is asserted.

title: Scalping — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Scalping describes attempts to capture small price movements over short holding periods.
summary: Scalping describes attempts to capture small price movements over short holding periods. Execution and costs can outweigh gross gains.

title: Volume Profile — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A volume profile groups recorded volume into price bins over a chosen interval.
summary: A volume profile groups recorded volume into price bins over a chosen interval. Its point of control is the highest-volume bin in that sample, not a forecast of where price must return.

title: VWAP — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: VWAP is the average observed trading price weighted by volume over a stated period.
summary: VWAP is the average observed trading price weighted by volume over a stated period. Price above or below it describes the sample; the relationship alone does not establish future direction.

title: Ichimoku Cloud — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Ichimoku Cloud displays several historical-price calculations with differing lookbacks and plotting offsets.
summary: Ichimoku Cloud displays several historical-price calculations with differing lookbacks and plotting offsets. Its Kumo cloud and other lines are chart conventions, not observations of future prices.

title: Elliott Wave Theory — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Elliott wave theory interprets price patterns using impulse and corrective wave counts.
summary: Elliott wave theory interprets price patterns using impulse and corrective wave counts. Different counts can fit the same observations; a chosen count does not establish a reliable forecast.

title: Wyckoff Method — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: The Wyckoff method interprets price and volume through phases such as accumulation, markup, distribution and markdown.
summary: The Wyckoff method interprets price and volume through phases such as accumulation, markup, distribution and markdown. Those labels describe a framework rather than verified institutional intentions.

title: Market Maker — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A market maker posts bid and ask quotes under venue rules to facilitate trading.
summary: A market maker posts bid and ask quotes under venue rules to facilitate trading. A quoted spread is not guaranteed profit, and obligations vary by market.

title: Dark Pool — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A non-displayed trading venue where orders generally do not appear in public pre-trade quotes.
summary: A non-displayed trading venue where orders generally do not appear in public pre-trade quotes. Not every off-exchange trade is a dark-pool trade.

title: Slippage — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Slippage is the difference between a stated reference price and an actual execution price.
summary: Slippage is the difference between a stated reference price and an actual execution price. It can be favorable or adverse; volatile conditions, limited liquidity and delays may increase it.

title: Impermanent Loss — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Impermanent loss compares the value of a liquidity-provider position with simply holding the original tokens.
summary: Impermanent loss compares the value of a liquidity-provider position with simply holding the original tokens. The difference depends on the pool design and relative prices; fees and incentives also matter.

title: Yield Farming — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: An informal term for seeking fees, interest or token incentives through DeFi protocols.
summary: An informal term for seeking fees, interest or token incentives through DeFi protocols. Reward rates, token prices, withdrawal terms and contract risks affect the result.

title: Flash Crash — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: A very rapid price decline, sometimes followed by a partial or full recovery.
summary: A very rapid price decline, sometimes followed by a partial or full recovery. Its causes and later path require event-specific evidence.

title: Circuit Breaker — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki

summary: A fraud scheme in which promoters use false or misleading claims to inflate an asset's price and sell their holdings at inflated prices, exposing later buyers to losses.

title: Risk-Reward Ratio — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: The risk-reward ratio compares a trade's planned loss with its planned gain.
summary: The risk-reward ratio compares a trade's planned loss with its planned gain. A 1:3 ratio means a planned $1 loss for a potential $3 gain; it does not guarantee those fills or establish a universal professional minimum.

title: Drawdown — Explanation & Learning Exercise | TradeHQ Wiki
description: Drawdown measures a decline from a previously observed peak to a later lower value, including an unfinished decline.
summary: Drawdown measures a decline from a previously observed peak to a later lower value, including an unfinished decline. Maximum drawdown is the largest such decline in a specified sample, not a ceiling on future loss.

summary: Backtesting applies stated rules to historical data to examine hypothetical results. It can reveal problems with an idea but does not validate future performance; look-ahead, survivorship and overfitting bias matter.
